title: Understanding Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is often preferred over squared loss in classification problems. Can you think of why this might be the case?

title: Properties of Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is particularly useful for binary classification problems. It measures the difference between two probability distributions - the true distribution and the predicted distribution. How does this relate to logistic regression?

title: Squared Loss in Classification
text: Squared loss is more commonly used in regression problems where the output is continuous. Why might it not be suitable for classification problems?

title: Comparing Loss Functions
text: Consider the behavior of squared loss and cross-entropy loss when the predicted probability is close to $$0$$ or $$1$$. Which loss function is more sensitive to these predictions?

hintAnswer: It helps in better distinguishing between classes.
title: Sensitivity to Predictions
text: Cross-entropy loss is more sensitive to predictions that are close to $$0$$ or $$1$$. This sensitivity helps in adjusting the model parameters more effectively. Why is this important in classification tasks?
choices: It helps in better distinguishing between classes.
